newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI B SHARES UP ON STRONG YITAI COAL DEBUT.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI B SHARES UP ON STRONG YITAI COAL DEBUT.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares ended up on Friday on healthy trading volume, buoyed by buying of newly listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal Co Ltd, brokers said.
Yitai Coal closed at $0.470, up $0.063 or 15.48 percent compared with an offer price of $0.407.
The B index rose 0.741 points or 1.0 percent to 74.923 points with turnover of $25.726 million compared with $7.132 million on Thursday.
Foreign capital was seen entering the market, chasing after newly-listed B shares, brokers said.

Brokers said the rise in trading volume could be a sign the B share market was starting a new upward trend, due to improved sentiment on talk of new government moves to reform state firms, which could boost some listed companies.
The recent strength of H shares, shares of Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong, could also carry over into the Shanghai B share market, they said.

"The H share market should have a rest after sharp rises over the past few weeks, so the B shares will rise on fresh inflow of capital," one local broker said. Of 47 B shares, 42 traded with 30 up, six flat and six down.
Shanghai Diesel Engine Co was the second biggest gainer after Yitai Coal on a technical rebound, surging $0.024 or 9.68 percent to $0.272.
Domestic currency A shares rose on enlarged trading volume, and the market would rise further if there is no negative news, brokers said.
The A index gained 6.988 points or 0.56 percent to 1,262.179 points on turnover of 5.728 billion yuan against 3.074 billion yuan on Thursday.
The SSE30 blue chip rose 71.530 points or 1.91 percent to 3,820.534 points.
Guangzhou Shipyard was the star on institutional buying, soaring 0.46 yuan or 10.04 percent to 5.04 yuan.
